result:
All three bugs are fixed:

1. **`src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts`** — `updateEndpoint` used `...(input.enabled && { enabled: input.enabled })`, which evaluates to `false` (a no-op spread) whenever `enabled: false` was passed, so switching an endpoint off never persisted. Changed to check `input.enabled === undefined`. Since `enqueueForOrg` in `webhook-service.ts` already skips disabled endpoints, this alone also fixes the "no new deliveries while off" symptom.

2. **`src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts`** — the delivery job checked for a missing endpoint but not a disabled one, so pre-queued deliveries for a switched-off endpoint were still marked delivered. Added a check that marks the delivery failed when `!endpoint.enabled`.

3. **`src/server/services/webhook-service.ts`** — `createWebhook` computed the plan-limit usage as `live.filter(e => e.enabled).length`, letting a workspace dodge the limit by disabling an endpoint first. Changed to count all endpoints (`existing.length`) regardless of enabled state.

Full test suite (617 tests) and `tsc --noEmit` both pass clean.
